claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 typically has significant porosity.
Porosity in conventional ZrB2 leads to structural failure during exposure to corrosive liquid plating baths.
Adding approximately 5 wt% MoSi2 to ZrB2 will permit densification below 2300 °C.
MoSi2 will act as a transient liquid-forming sintering aid in ZrB2.
MoSi2 reacts with the ZrB2 matrix to generate a transient liquid phase during sintering.
The transient liquid phase enhances particle rearrangement and mass transport.
The transient liquid phase accelerates densification by enhancing diffusion and grain-boundary migration.
Liquid-phase-assisted sintering with MoSi2 produces improved densification and reduced residual porosity.
Reduced porosity minimizes preferential sites for plating-liquid infiltration and corrosion.
Reduced infiltration and corrosion improve the long-term structural integrity of ZrB2 in liquid plating baths.
At 1800–2100 °C, MoSi2-doped ZrB2 will achieve densification similar to or better than conventional ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C.
MoSi2-doped ZrB2 will contain fewer and smaller pores than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
MoSi2-doped ZrB2 will resist corrosion-induced hole formation better than conventionally prepared ZrB2 during prolonged plating-bath exposure.
The modified ceramic can retain a single-phase composition after addition and reactive sintering of approximately 5 wt% MoSi2.
Transient-liquid behavior depends sensitively on processing details.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis introduces 5 wt% MoSi2 and proposes reaction with the ZrB2 matrix, yet the boundary requires maintenance of a single-phase composition. It does not specify how the additive and any reaction products are eliminated, dissolved into one phase, or otherwise prevented from leaving secondary phases.
